name: Cyclic Group
definition: A cyclic group is a group generated by a single element such that every element can be expressed as a power of that generator.

defining_equations.explanation: a is the generator, n is the order of the group, and e is the identity element. The relation means applying a n times returns to identity.
This is the set of all elements obtained by successive powers of the generator a.

visuals.description: The Cayley graph of C5 shows five elements arranged in a cycle. Each directed edge represents multiplication by one generator, so repeated movement along the graph cycles through all group elements and returns to the start.

origin_history: Cyclic groups emerged from modular arithmetic and periodic structures. They were formalized in the 18th and 19th centuries, especially through Gauss's work on modular arithmetic and roots of unity.
importance: Cyclic groups form the simplest class of groups and act as building blocks for more complex algebraic systems. They connect number theory, algebra, and harmonic analysis through modular arithmetic, roots of unity, and periodic structure. They are widely used in cryptography, signal processing, modular arithmetic, and coding theory.
research_trends: Cyclic groups are used in group-equivariant neural networks, where symmetry constraints improve model efficiency and generalization. They are also central to spectral learning and Fourier-based AI models, where periodic structures help represent signals and structured data.
intuition: A cyclic group behaves like a clock where repeated steps eventually return to the starting point.
minimal_example: C5 = {0,1,2,3,4} under addition mod 5. Example: 3 + 4 congruent to 2 modulo 5.

n = 5
def op(a, b):
